evidence.summary: Changing different input features produced different score changes, indicating that the final output depends on multiple features rather than a single dominant feature.
The clearance score changed across controlled shipment queries, showing that it is calculated from the supplied feature combination rather than being a fixed value.

The APPROVE or DECLINE output varied with the queried manifests. The observations suggest a relationship between the generated score and the final decision, although the exact decision boundary is not fully known.
No single tested feature was sufficient to explain all observed score and decision changes. This makes a simple one-feature rule unlikely.
Seven black-box queries are not enough to determine the exact model type, feature weights, interaction terms, or precise APPROVE/DECLINE threshold.
